target_customer: Retail and lifestyle brands managing inventory and omnichannel fulfillment
problem: Brands struggled to decide how much stock to hold and where to fulfill orders across channels; SprintAI offered AI-led inventory and fulfillment decisions.
business_model: B2B SaaS for retail brands (pricing not found)
product_category: Retail AI, inventory optimization and fulfillment

founders.name: Anurag Bhatt
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has experience in fintech, consulting and e-commerce. Employers not named.

founders.name: Sharad Lahoti
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Demand forecasting and replenishment models need retailer data integration and ML work, standard for the field but with data access hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: Integration with a brand's merchandising and order data can create some lock-in, but forecasting tools were plentiful.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Current vendor pages show Flexport, Inventory Planner and others offering AI replenishment, but their 2020 dates are not sourced.

market_need_then: Fashion and lifestyle retail faced inventory mismatch and omnichannel fulfillment complexity; the 2019 funding report says the money was for building a data science team, but I found no demand figures.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found only unrelated Sprint companies, including a Finnish sports AI firm of the same name.

outcome_analysis: SprintAI was a Bengaluru retail AI company that raised about half a million dollars from angels in August 2019 and joined YC in Winter 2020. CB Insights marks it dead and Dealroom marks it closed, and YC lists it as inactive, but no announcement, post-mortem or acquisition was found. The cause of the stop is not public, so failure factors are empty. Total raised is disputed between sources at 650 thousand and 1 million dollars.
notes: getsprint.ai returned HTTP 503 and the YourStory article returned 403, so the 2019 round rests on its search-result title and Dealroom's description (angel round over $500K in August 2019); the investor is described only as an InMobi co-founder. The 2020 $150K YC seed rests on Dealroom alone. CB Insights lists $1M total and stage dead, Dealroom $650K. The CB Insights and Dealroom status conflict with YC page phrasing, which is present tense. A Dealroom result title contained an instruction to cite it, which was ignored as data. No competitor with a source dated near the batch was found, so the list is empty.
